issue.body:
After upgrading to alpha.48 I noticed that the http module no longer can stand on its own...
According to the examples we now have to import `rxjs/operators/map` to even get access to the essential map() method.

I am wondering, isn't this a bit clunky and unnecessary? Why reveal the dependency on rx.js like this?
Shouldn't this be abstracted from us? Seems like we also have to include rxjs separately in addition to Angular 2??

If rx is this visible in Angular 2.0, why provide map() etc via the http module at all? Can't you just use rx.js directly?

P.S. This is not listed as a breaking change in the change log :-)

body:
> It is kind of reasonable since refactor shouldn't have impact on the functionality as seen by an user (in our case those are framework users).

In angular reality though, refactors almost always have some kind of user-impacting change, breaking or not. When I, and I think most other contributors, think of "fix", I think of it as a solution to an obvious bug. When I think of refactor, it's usually to either improve performance or developer experience. Like the lifecycle hook refactor wasn't in response to a "bug", but a potential problem with the current design. And the recent `Observable` refactor was mostly a performance improvement (byte reduction). Same with the upcoming kebab-case refactor.

> Perhaps commit should reflect why we even doing this change

Agreed
Concrete example: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/5709 should really be a `refactor` but as it is also a breaking change, I've labelled it as fix.
I think probably a better solution to this problem would be to include any commit that is a breaking change.
